advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add behavioral exit-code assertions for the newly documented codes 3 (fsck-recover --detect-only on a stale rebase), 4 (validate critical health), and 12 (review-plan --status stale), executing the CLI and asserting the real returncode, rather than only asserting the code number appears in the doc text.
evidence: test_codes_3_4_12_75_78_are_documented only greps the codes table: `codes = set(re.findall(r"^\| `(\d+)`", _text(), re.MULTILINE))` then `assert code in codes` — it verifies the code appears as a heading, not that any command emits it

Code 75 IS behaviorally pinned: tests/unit/test_store.py:100 `assert ei.value.returncode == 75`; code 3's no-rebase path is pinned at tests/interfaces/contracts/test_store_compat_gate.py:259 `assert cp.returncode == 0` — but the stale-rebase => 3 path is not

Code 12 appears in source only at src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:510 `return 0 if status["ok"] else 12` with no test asserting exit 12; code 4 (validate 1/5 critical) has no executable exit-code assertion (search found no test emitting 4)

docs/exit-codes.md:6 claims the doc is the source of truth for 'which code each subcommand emits'; ticket f0ff notes the sole historical exit-code regression was caught by a behavioral test, not by documentation
advisory.finding: The newly documented exit codes 3 (fsck-recover --detect-only on a stale rebase), 4 (validate critical health), and 12 (review-plan --status stale/absent) are asserted only as text present in docs/exit-codes.md, never behaviorally: no test executes the CLI and asserts the emitted process exit code equals the documented code. A drifted or wrong code claim for these arms passes CI, which is the exact regression class this doc+test exists to catch.
scenarios: review-plan --status regressed to return 1 instead of 12 on a stale attestation — both conformance tests stay green
validate's critical-health bucket stops emitting 4 — no test fails
